status: Fixed after arm S (protocol-roi-20261111.json) and before any zero-mean output. One arm; no refit after outcomes.
motivation: Arm S passed all 16 quality rows but its offsets are all negative (mean about -1 QP), which raised authored rate to 127.4/130.4 Mb/s and failed the 130 screen on Michael1800. x265 AQ is itself zero-mean per frame (strength*(qp_adj - avg_adj)); a luminance term that is also zero-mean redistributes bits from bright to dark blocks instead of adding them.
hypothesis: The same dark-block offset, balanced by a uniform positive offset on the remaining blocks, keeps the shadow-tail repair while holding the rate near the retained baseline.
baseline: Identical to protocol-roi-20261111.json (retained single-pass115 qg32 CLI options, translated verbatim; gates E0/E1 already passed with the same harness logic).

arm_Z.map_input: The encoder's own input frame, every frame independently. No reference, F or C error enters the map.
arm_Z.dark_selection: As arm S: block mean Y' -> ST 2084 nits < 1.0 nit.
arm_Z.other_offset: +min(3, 3*c/(1-c)) QP on every non-dark block, c = that frame's dark-block fraction; zero frame mean whenever c <= 0.5
arm_Z.encoding: Dark runs listed first, then one full-frame region with the positive offset; libx265.c applies the first listed region on overlap. Positive qoffset is round(offset*1e6)/63e6.

qualification: Same as arm S (qualify_spatial_control.py --qg-size 32 with AQ and QP-group receipts, frozen author, quality pipeline).
bar: Unchanged strict quality bar and unchanged 130 Mb/s authored-average screen.
